title: Unify lint/test scripts and introduce dependency-guard presubmit
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Added a repo-wide dependency-guard presubmit job and consolidated language lint/test scripts into tooling/scripts for consistent CI behavior. No runtime changes. Improves CI hygiene and reduces duplicated scripts.
description:
Motivation: Over time we accumulated ad-hoc lint/test shell scripts across packages and multiple slightly-different GH Action job definitions. This made it hard to keep presubmit checks consistent and complicated adding a single dependency audit step across the mono-repo. This PR centralizes lint/test invocations into tooling/scripts (single entrypoints for node/python/go), removes duplicated GH Action fragments, and adds a dependency-guard presubmit workflow that performs license/dep-variance checks and blocks merges on suspicious changes.

What I changed: - Added tooling/scripts/{node,python,go}-check.sh wrapper scripts that normalize env, node/python versions, and exit codes. - Replaced in-repo ad-hoc npm/yarn calls with npm run tooling:check (node) or python -m tooling.check (python) where applicable. - Introduced .github/workflows/dependency-guard.yml: a lightweight presubmit job that runs dependency-guard (open-source wrapper with in-repo allowlist) plus a periodic audit schedule. - Consolidated existing lint/test GH Action fragments into .github/actions/standard-checks (composite action) and updated workflows to call it. - Removed duplicate scripts and updated README/tooling docs. - Small cleanup: fixed mismatched eslint configs, aligned jest thresholds, and added an ignore whitelist for legacy third-party transitive deps.

Checklist: - [x] Centralize scripts and update package.json/workspace entries - [x] Add dependency-guard workflow and baseline allowlist - [x] Update CircleCI->GH Actions translation for two legacy jobs - [x] Run full monorepo CI and fix lint/test failures - [x] Add docs entry under docs/dev/ci.md describing new presubmit flow

Rollout plan: Merge to main, watch the presubmit job for 48 hours; non-blocking periodic audit runs will surface transitive changes. Any blocked PRs can request the allowlist update via SUP-89.

Testing: Ran full suite on remote runner, fixed three flaky tests surfaced by standardized env. Dependency-guard was run against a historical baseline and the allowlist recorded in tooling/dep-allowlist.json.

Notes: This is intentionally conservative — dependency-guard is configured to block only high-severity or license violations by default; team can opt-in to stricter mode later. The composite action is lightweight to keep matrix times low.
